ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: US fires top military planner over alleged leaks: reports.
The United States has fired a top military planner, US media reported, with some outlets saying the dismissal was due to the officer allegedly leaking classified information. Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was removed from his role as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Staff, US media reported on Wednesday, citing unnamed sources. CBS and Fox both reported that Sylvia’s dismissal was related to leaks, with the former citing a Pentagon official as saying the general failed three polygraphs about sharing classified information with the media.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that could hold the key to forming a government after an inconclusive election. Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation into allegations of fraud but cautioned against stigmatising the entire Arab Israeli community, who voted at unprecedented rates.

- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: 'Not related to defence': Govt responds to Fazl's remarks about Makkah pact countries' meeting in Tehran.
Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the meeting was not related to defence. Hence, Asif said his presence was not required, while Naqvi explained the reasons for his participation. The remarks came after the JUI-F chief questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at the meeting.
